normalized_quote_exact_with_supplied_bra: We noticed in the Detroit Jou[r]nal the ope[ning] of a new House in that city, under the [name] of the American Hotel, by Mr. Griswold, [which] will doubtless be very interesting & agree[able] [n]ews to travellers who may have occasion [to stop] at Detroit. Detroit has been far behind [other] places in the west in its public Houses.— [We h]ave a number of good houses in this city— [as it i]s to be. The Sauganash has been re[paired,] fitted up and furnished with neatness and [taste,] and so far as it goes, will[, we have no] [doubt, ] be found just the thing, and there are oth[ers] [w]hose qualities are well known. But there [is no] e[st]ablishment here sufficiently extensive to [satisf]y the demands of those who resort here for [busin]ess, or curiosity, or pleasure. There is [a] new house building in Kinzie's addition [to be] named we understand, the "Lake Hous[e]." [There] should be a house about double the size [of that] latter, erected this side of the river about [the ce]ntre of Lake Street or in that vicinity.
old_function_fragment: The same paragraph fixes its scale by comparison: the editor wants a house 'about double the size of that latter' put up on the south side of the river 'about the centre of Lake Street', which tells you this one was not yet the largest thing in Chicago and that nothing stood at the site he proposed.
new_function_fragment: The same paragraph contains an editorial proposal for a house 'about double the size of that latter' near the centre of Lake Street on this side of the river. The comparison expresses a desired relative hotel size; it supplies no measured dimensions or July construction stage and does not establish the Lake House's rank among existing buildings. The proposal is not an existing-house observation and does not prove that the suggested site was vacant.
old_claim_interpretation_fragment: That is a PROPOSAL and not a building — nothing stood there — but it fixes the Lake House's scale by comparison (a house double it would be the town's largest) and it tells you where the commercial centre of gravity was felt to be: the middle of Lake Street, south of the river.
new_claim_interpretation_fragment: That is an EDITORIAL PROPOSAL, not an observed building or a measurement of the Lake House. It expresses a desired relative hotel size on the south side near the centre of Lake Street, but supplies no measured Lake House dimensions, rank among existing buildings, amount of work completed, or roof/storey stage. Nor does it establish that the proposed site was vacant. Do not turn the proposal into an existing house or use it to size the July 1835 shell.
